blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Write-time re-open 2026-08-08 against official Zephyr documentation, the still-current v2.3.0 source commit 67c5f53b878fef41fb5e74c4382d5b7a2f37fd8a, and native-chain HF11 block 837231 (2026-08-08 19:36:16 UTC; hash 9e024c96ef5e31b25daa407c0715a43e74f9fdfc18c258bf4c50077ef15f160d). ZSD is one of four native Zephyr asset types; the official docs list the EVM bridge as testnet-only, so no production wrapper exposure is identified. Same-asset ZSD sends map to STABLE_TRANSFER in cryptonote_tx_utils.cpp; the reviewed consensus and wallet paths expose no address blacklist, holder freeze, seize, privileged burn, or issuer/admin transfer-pause path. wallet2.cpp freeze() only marks a locally held transfer/key image, while daemon bans are host/subnet controls. The failure domain is Zephyr chain consensus and its oracle inputs, not a token-level issuer. No direct blacklistability established.

oracleRisk.summary: Zephyr documents ZSD as a Djed-style stablecoin backed by one protocol-wide ZEPH reserve with a 400% minimum reserve ratio; current public materials do not identify the production oracle provider set or failure handling.

branchApplicability.rationale: Zephyr describes ZSD as a protocol reserve liability backed by ZEPH, with minting gated by a system-wide reserve ratio. Users do not open borrower-specific collateral positions, so the reviewed design exposes no market-specific collateral or liquidation branches to inventory.
